items.title: Punjab faces greater threat from other provinces than 'neighbouring countries': CM Maryam
items.description: Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz on Saturday said the province faced a greater security threat from “neighbouring provinces than from neighbouring countries”, stressing that terrorism entered Punjab through its provincial borders. Speaking at an AI technology event in Lahore, the chief minister said: “The unfortunate thing is that the threat [Punjab] faces comes less from my neighbouring countries and more from my neighbouring provinces.” “Terrorism enters Punjab from there. Everyone has their eyes on Punjab, but, thank God, Punjab remains safe. The kind of threats we face come from all our provincial borders,” she said. The chief minister asserted that there had been a significant improvement in the law and order situation since her government came to power in 2024. She identified organised crime and religious intolerance as some of the main challenges that Punjab faced. In an apparent reference to the now-banned Tehreek-i-Labbaik Pakistan (TLP), CM Maryam said some groups “spread hatred under the cover of religion” and were “political parties in reality”. She went on to state that religious events were now held peacefully, compared to the situation of “religious polarisation” a couple of years ago. Maryam said Punjab was now the country’s “most AI-enabled province” and had invested billions of rupees in technology and security to protect and strengthen it. She said that when she assumed office, she discovered that terrorists possessed more advanced technology than the government, including night-vision cameras, and were carrying out attacks with carefully devised plans. “Thank God, we now have a complete system in place,” she said, adding that cameras had been made bulletproof because terrorists used to target them. Thermal cameras and drones had also been deployed at checkpoints and joint checkpoints to strengthen security and protect people. The Punjab CM recalled that attacks on checkpoints had previously resulted in the deaths of five people and, at times, as many as 10. “Attacks still happen, but the loss of life has been significantly reduced,” she said, attributing the improvement to investment in fortification and technology. Referring to the katcha areas , Maryam said they had previously been a hub of terrorism and crime, including kidnappings for ransom and honey traps. “With the support we have received from the military and the Punjab government, and with the cooperation of the Sindh government, the situation has now changed. The area has become largely crime-free, and the writ of the state has been established,” she declared. The chief minister also said she had decided “a few days ago” to take action against elements involved in corruption. “I am not talking about government ranks or referring to police ranks … I am talking about us as a nation. We have become so accustomed to corruption that it has become part of our daily routine,” she said. Maryam noted her government had also established a system to ensure immediate action against corrupt elements. “If people do not trust their state, that country can never move forward,” she remarked. PTI condemns CM Maryam’s remarks PTI Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram strongly condemned Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz’s remarks that a neighbouring province posed a greater security threat to her than India, saying the statement was reckless and reflected a disturbing tendency to view a national security challenge through the narrow lens of provincial politics. In a statement issued by the party’s Central Media Department, Waqas said Maryam’s remarks reflected an attempt to view national security through the prism of personal, familial and provincial interests. “Such selective political narratives are highly irresponsible, particularly at a time when terrorism remains a national challenge, with no part of the country completely safe from the threat. Combating terrorism requires unity, collective responsibility and cooperation among all federating units, rather than attempts to pit one province against another or exploit the issue for narrow political and provincial interests,” he said. Waqas said such remarks were not unprecedented, recalling that Maryam’s uncle, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, had also made a similar statement in the past when he appealed to terrorists to spare Punjab. He described that stance as deeply irresponsible, saying it was interpreted as an appeal to direct terrorist activities towards other parts of the country rather than Punjab. He reminded Maryam that Pakistan’s security challenges could not be addressed by blaming one province while ignoring broader national and regional realities. Waqas added that the country needed leadership capable of thinking beyond provincial boundaries and treating every Pakistani citizen equally. Additional reporting by Ikram Junaidi

items.title: Décès de Fatou Ndiaye, dite Madame Turpin : une perte immense pour le mouvement féministe sénégalais
items.description: Le Réseau Siggil Jigéen (RSJ) annonce avec tristesse le rappel à Dieu de sa directrice exécutive, Fatou Ndiaye, dite Madame Turpin, décédée ce samedi 5 septembre. Durant de nombreuses années, Fatou Ndiaye a été en première ligne dans la lutte contre les violences basées sur le genre et pour la défense des droits des femmes. Son dévouement et ses combats pour la cause féminine resteront à jamais gravés dans la mémoire du Réseau Siggil Jigéen, de ses collaborateurs ainsi que de tous ceux qui ont eu l’occasion de la côtoyer. L’enterrement est prévu ce dimanche 6 septembre à 10 heures, à Yoff. En ces douloureux moments, le Réseau Siggil Jigéen présente ses sincères condoléances à la famille éplorée, à ses amis et connaissances, ainsi qu’à l’ensemble du mouvement féministe sénégalais. F. NGOM

items.title: Ex-IGP Adamu replaces Amgba as SDP Governorship Candidate in Nasarawa
items.description: By Edwin Phillip, Lafia Former Inspector General of Police (IGP), Muhammed Abubakar Adamu, has emerged as the gubernatorial candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP) for the 2027 general election, replacing Musa Adamu Angba, who had withdrawn from the race. Adamu emerged following a direct primary through an affirmation voice vote on Saturday, as monitored by the Independent Electoral Commission (INEC) in accordance with the Electoral Act and the commission’s guidelines. Speaking shortly after his emergence, the former IGP said that having gone around the state, he has taken notes of the lack of basic social amenities and the lack of roads and health care facilities in the local communities. He said, “We will not neglect social amenities that are required. We’ve gone round the state; we have seen all the roads that are in the hinterlands are neglected. We’ll make sure that we take care of that. We’ll provide healthcare that is needed not only in the urban cities but also in the rural areas.” ​He described Nasarawa as an agrarian state, with vast expanses of land that is conducive for agriculture, which his administration, if elected, will invest in to feed the people of Nasarawa and the country as a whole. “On mineral resources, the way it is being handled now, the way it is being exploited, is not to the benefit of the people of the state. “We are going to look into the way it has been handled and make sure that the benefit comes to the people,” he said. The SDP governorship candidate promised to undertake a campaign that will speak to the issues in every ward and local government area of the state. ​”During the campaign, we are going to be specific; we shall be specific in all that we will do and tell our people what we are going to do word-by-word, local government-by-local government.” Appreciating the party and the people, the confidence rests on him. Muhammed Abubakar Adamu said he is delighted with the outcome of the primary election that brought him in, promising to work round the clock to make the state better than he met it. ​”We are going to work tirelessly to change the bad governance that is taking place in Nasarawa State for the better, Insha’Allah. We will not allow the government to fall into the hands of another bad person. “We will work with all the people of Nasarawa State and our supporting partners and development partners all over the country and the world to bring development to Nasarawa State,” he expressed. Also speaking, the presidential candidate of the SDP, Prince Adewole Adebayo, said that the party’s governorship candidate needs no introduction to the people of Nasarawa, having led the Nigerian Police Force with discipline, integrity and commitment to the rule of law, which has made Nasarawa State and Nigeria proud. He urged the residents of the state to vote for candidates of the party in all positions. “It’s your leeway; we can be able to give them what it takes to be able to discharge their responsibility as leaders at various levels to rescue our nation from monsters and criminal elements. He, however, assured that, judging from the governorship election in Osun State, the Independent Electoral Commission (INEC) is seen as a neutral umpire who is ready to give Nigerians a free, fair and credible election. ​”I want to assure you today that we have an INEC that is responsible and responsive to their responsibility. I want to assure you, if you are ready to exercise your franchise and elect candidates of our party, today you have an INEC that will declare your candidate.” “The onus is on you to exercise your franchise, to exercise your will to elect your leaders. It has happened in Osun; it will happen in Nasarawa State,” he added. Reacting to Adamu’s emergence as the SDP govership candidate in Nasarawa State, high chief Otaru Douglas, Director, Media and Strategic Communications For: IGP Mohammed Abubakar Adamu (Rtd) Campaign Organisation, in a press statement, said that today’s affirmation has finally put to rest the endless speculations and rumours that his principal will not be on the ballot. “The people have shown uncommon resilience and commitment to changing the governance narrative of our dear state. They have rejected politics of intimidation and inducement and have chosen competence, experience, integrity and proven leadership.” “To the good people of Nasarawa State, this is just the beginning. IGP Mohammed Abubakar Adamu (Rtd) represents security, order, inclusion and purposeful governance. The journey to rescue and rebuild Nasarawa State has officially begun,” he added The post Ex-IGP Adamu replaces Amgba as SDP Governorship Candidate in Nasarawa appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Boulkiemdé : Ramongo intensifie la lutte anti vectorielle contre les moustiques et l’insalubrité
items.description: BURKINA-BOULKIEMDE-RAMONGO-JNLAV-EDITION-2 Boulkiemdé : Ramongo intensifie la lutte anti vectorielle contre les moustiques et l’insalubrité Ramongo, 5 sept. 2026 (AIB) – La commune de Ramongo a entamé samedi, le deuxième passage des Journées nationales de lutte anti vectorielle (JNLAV), à travers une campagne de sensibilisation et des opérations de salubrité visant à prévenir le paludisme et les autres maladies à transmission vectorielle. L’activité, présidée par la Présidente de la délégation spéciale (PDS) de Ramongo, Kouna Yvette Saré, a enregistré une forte mobilisation de la population, avec une prédominance des femmes. L'espace de la mairie, le yaar et le marché sont les lieux retenus pour le nettoyage. Pour cette première journée, les participants se sont mobilisés pour assainir l’espace de la mairie et le yaar de Ramongo, munis notamment de dabas, pioches, machettes, râteaux, brouettes et autres matériels nécessaires aux travaux de nettoyage. La sensibilisation a été lancée par la PDS, avec l’appui des majors des CSPS de Kamsi, Harouna Guiro, et de Ramongo, Kora Adama Nignan, ainsi que du responsable du Service des Eaux et Assainissement de la mairie, Hamidou Kaboré. Les échanges ont porté sur la couverture des récipients, le débroussaillement autour des habitations, des services et des lieux publics, la vidange des eaux stagnantes, la destruction des gîtes larvaires et la bonne gestion des déchets. Les populations ont également été sensibilisées sur la nécessité de maintenir leurs cadres de vie et de travail propres afin de réduire les conditions favorables à la prolifération des moustiques. Les participants ont soulevé des préoccupations concernant notamment la sous-utilisation des moustiquaires imprégnées par certaines personnes qui en bénéficient, ainsi que l’automédication de nombreux enfants par leurs parents au lieu de les conduire dans les formations sanitaires pour une meilleure prise en charge. Des réponses satisfaisantes ont été apportées à ces préoccupations au cours des échanges. La mobilisation a également enregistré la participation des appelés à l’Immersion patriotique obligatoire de la commune, qui se sont joints à la population aux côtés des autorités pour les activités de sensibilisation et de salubrité. L’un d’eux s’est félicité de l’initiative présidentielle ayant permis la tenue de cette immersion et a invité ses camarades à rester mobilisés autour des idéaux du leader de la Révolution progressiste populaire. Des individus dont les cadres de vie présentaient un niveau d’insalubrité préoccupant ont, par ailleurs, été interpellés et sensibilisés sur place par les autorités compétentes. La PDS Kouna Yvette Saré s’est déclarée satisfaite de la mobilisation et a invité les populations à maintenir durablement leurs cadres de vie et de travail sains. Après les rencontres préparatoires tenues dans les formations sanitaires et à la mairie avec la PDS, les activités des JNLAV se poursuivent dimanche au marché de Ramongo. Les gestes simples d’aujourd’hui contribuent à garantir une meilleure santé demain. Ensemble, luttons contre les moustiques pour une communauté saine et sans paludisme. Agence d'information du Burkina LO/PB/AS/ATA

items.title: Lawyers, prosecutors fume over abandoned 26-year-old Upper West High court project
items.description: Members of the legal fraternity in the Upper West Region, alongside state prosecutors, have registered fierce displeasure over the stalled construction of the multi-million-cedi regional High Court complex, describing the deserted site as a “cemetery” after two decades of dashed hopes. The regional leadership of the Ghana Bar Association (GBA) and the Office of the Attorney General revealed that despite high-profile inspections and firm commitments given by national delegations, the three-storey court structure has once again been abandoned by the contractor, leaving the regional capital without a single purpose-built modern courtroom. Visiting the deserted project grounds on Friday, legal practitioners expressed dismay that equipment had been packed off, leaving open gates, uninstalled fittings exposed to theft, and fresh paint peeling off exterior walls just three months after application. Chairman of the Ghana Bar Association in the Upper West Region, Siddique Ubeidu, warned that members fear for their lives daily due to the worsening decay of the makeshift buildings currently housing justice delivery in the region. “You will recall that this work was started almost 20 years ago, and it has been one reason or excuse for another,” Siddique Ubeidu stated. “Our national executive committee of the GBA was here on the 1st of April and was given assurances that within three to four months, the building would be completed. Subsequently, the Chief Justice sent another team led by a Supreme Court judge, Justice Yonny Kulendi, alongside all directors from the Judicial Service, assuring us it would be available for use within two to three months.” “Here we are today, 4th September, and the place is a cemetery. If you look at the way they packed their equipment, there is no sign that they will be back anytime soon. What is even more worrying is that the paint done less than three months ago has started peeling off, pointing to the suspect quality of the work,” he added. According to the bar president, a visit inside the operational Wa Circuit Court exposes severe structural deterioration that poses a daily hazard to occupants. “We feel very depressed and disappointed, and we even fear for our lives. You can see gaping, life-threatening cracks inside the judge’s chambers and the courtroom. Staff have no offices and compete with litigants inside the courtroom, even eating their meals there. “Years ago, former Chief Justice Sophia Akuffo came to town and threatened to shut the court down due to its state, yet nothing was done while the population grew,” Siddique Ubeidu lamented. Principal State Attorney, Upper West Region, Saeed Abdul-Shakur, described the state of affairs as a national embarrassment that borders on institutional neglect of the region. “It didn’t take China 20 years to build the Three Gorges Dam, nor Dubai 10 years to build the Burj Khalifa. Why is it taking a whole nation 20 years to set up just a three-storey building for a court complex?” Saeed Abdul-Shakur queried. “We are serving 11 districts, yet the High Court, District Court, and Circuit Court are all operating out of colonial and temporary makeshift structures. We thought the visits by the Parliamentary Select Committee and the Chief Justice’s delegation meant light at the end of the tunnel, without knowing it was an oncoming train bound to crash the justice system. We cannot be delivering justice under trees,” the Principal State Attorney stated, stressing that lawyers and litigants travel from Accra, Kumasi, and Tamale to litigate in Wa. Weighing in on the missed schedules, Acting Secretary, Ghana Bar Association, Upper West Region, Crispin Wura-Sey Ziekah, warned that the continuous delays have left vital court infrastructure compromised. “Are we waiting for our courts to collapse before we complete this structure?” Crispin Wura-Sey Ziekah questioned. “At the District Court, a magistrate has to wait in his vehicle until proceedings are assembled before stepping inside. We were assured the new complex would be commissioned during the Bar Conference hosted here last year; it failed. We were promised we would start the new legal year this October in the complex, but the contractor has packed out completely, and the unsecured gates leave installations vulnerable to vandalism.” The legal practitioners have appealed directly to the Chief Justice, the Attorney General, and the Minister for Justice to step in and compel the contractor and project consultants back to site, demanding that the facility be operationalised to avert a catastrophe in the region’s makeshift courtrooms. Meanwhile, the contractor for the project, Project Seven Limited, has refuted claims that it has abandoned the site. A director of the company, Simon Sowah, speaking to JoyNews, said the company has unpaid certificates pending with the Judicial Service and central government. According to him, the company will return to the site once the government does the needful and settles its indebtedness.

items.title: Naqvi says new administrative units to be formed only with people's consent
items.description: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Saturday said that any new administrative units in the country would only be formed if the people voiced their support for such a move. Addressing the National Policy Dialogue in Lahore, he said, “Reset does not mean breaking the system. Under no circumstances does it mean breaking the system. It means that whatever is wrong should be changed.” Naqvi stressed that the changes should be brought through “political consensus” and “according to the will of our people”. He added that if the nation did not want the new administrative units, they would not be created. He emphasised that such a change could not be brought about only based on the will of an individual, a political party or a government. “And this would only happen if the people want it and consent to it,” he maintained. The interior minister called for a dialogue that would consider the positive and negative aspects of new units. “Draft a thing and present it to the people, asking them whether they accept it or not.” On the question of how many new administrative units should be created with what territorial limits, Naqvi emphasised the need to review their “benefits, methods and financial consequences”. “Most importantly, our parliament, experts and those people responsible for it should debate on it, and finally, we must seek our public’s opinion.” The minister clarified that his comments from last month were not about any particular political party, but rather about the “system” that has been in place since the country’s independence. Naqvi called for undertaking the proposed administrative reforms as per the Constitution. “It has to be done through democratic means.” “Under no circumstances are we ready to accept that we have become so incapable that we cannot reset this system,” he said, calling for political parties to hold deliberations on the matter. The interior minister asserted he would not abandon the idea, adding that many “emotional” speeches were being made about the administrative units. He urged politicians not to get emotional about the topic, adding that the change was not one that would happen overnight. The minister contended that the country’s administrative system had lost its effectiveness and its “impact is not reaching the public at all”. Acknowledging administrative issues, Naqvi said, “Even today, four out of every 10 children are not receiving the education they need. Today, only 55 per cent of the population has access to clean drinking water, and there are still two million cases pending in our courts.” These were the issues that the government was trying to rectify, he contended. Describing himself as the “biggest supporter of Islamabad province”, Naqvi called for the federal capital to receive its share of the National Finance Commission (NFC) Award. “Islamabad is the only city that does not get a single rupee from the budget of Pakistan,” he insisted, adding that declaring Islamabad a province would give its citizens their rights. The minister also highlighted the population factor in the disbursement of the NFC award, saying it remained an “incentive” for provinces. “That incentive is present till today, so are we waiting for that bomb to explode? […] Does this not need to be reset?” Naqvi further said, “Governments keep changing; policies keep changing; budgets come and go; and we keep making plans. But the biggest issue is how much we are able to deliver in the end.” He added that if, despite all the potential that Pakistan has, “we are still not getting the results, it is necessary to reset it (the system)”. Citing New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani as an example, Naqvi said the politicians who came to power as mayors knew their citizens and their problems the best. The minister stressed that the proposed reforms would aim to empower the people. He said a Sindhi would remain Sindhi and a Punjabi would remain Punjabi. “No one will be asked to surrender their identity,” he assured the public. He added that the discussion on the proposed reforms was not supposed to be based on generational, tribal or regional divides. “Its aim is improved governance, a competent system and bringing people closer to the government.” Concluding his address, Naqvi reiterated: “In no circumstances should we stray from the will of the people. All political parties will have to deliberate on this. It cannot be one person’s issue or one province’s decision.” He added, “If this is what the public wants, then it will happen no matter what.” IPP welcomes minister’s position on the creation of new provinces Istehkam-i-Pakistan Party (IPP) President Abdul Aleem Khan welcomed Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal’s stance on the creation of new provinces, saying the positive and well-reasoned views expressed by political leaders from different parties on the important national issue were encouraging. In a message posted on X, Aleem appreciated Iqbal’s position and said it was reassuring that political leaders at the national level were adopting a positive approach towards the creation of new provinces. He emphasised that new provinces should be created on the basis of administrative requirements and public convenience rather than linguistic or cultural considerations. The IPP president said the issue was not the concern of any single political party but an important matter concerning the future of the country and its people. He described the initiation of a serious political debate among national political parties on the issue as a positive development. Aleem added that differences of opinion were a hallmark of democracy, but all political parties should play a serious role in taking the debate on new provinces towards a logical conclusion rather than using it for political point-scoring. He further stated that the provincial assemblies of Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa had already passed resolutions in support of new provinces, while the division of quotas between rural and urban areas had been in place in Sindh since 1972. He said the creation of new administrative units could help resolve public issues more effectively and improve the efficiency of governance. “After nearly 80 years, the country needs to reorganise its administrative structure in line with present and future requirements. Istehkam-i-Pakistan Party has already supported the creation of Hazara province in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and is ready to engage with every political party and stakeholder on the issue of new provinces and listen to all viewpoints,” he said. In July, Naqvi had proposed a dialogue among all political parties to bring about reforms to the current governance system, while also calling for new provinces and urgent administrative reforms. His comments had ignited an animated debate across the country, with the PPP referring the question to its top decision-making forum, the Sindh chief minister flatly rejecting it, Lahore’s lawyers terming it unconstitutional and Sindhi nationalist groups demanding the minister’s resignation.

items.title: Premier League : Iliman Ndiaye éblouit l’Etihad Stadium pour ses débuts
items.description: Pour ses premiers pas sous le maillot de Manchester City, Iliman Ndiaye a connu une entrée réussie. Titulaire face à Coventry ce samedi à l’Etihad Stadium, l’international sénégalais a participé au succès des Citizens (1-0), décrochant ainsi une première victoire avec son nouveau club. Pas de round d’observation pour Iliman Ndiaye. Arrivé d’Everton en début de semaine, le nouveau numéro 7 des Sky Blues a immédiatement été lancé dans le onze de départ par Enzo Maresca. L’attaquant sénégalais, recruté pour apporter sa créativité et sa polyvalence au secteur offensif, a donc découvert sans attendre l’exigeante atmosphère de l’Etihad. Iliman n’a pas mis longtemps à se montrer dangereux. Dès la 19e minute, c’est lui qui provoque le premier carton jaune du match, fauché par Milan van Ewijk alors qu’il s’échappait sur une contre-attaque rapide. Tout au long de la rencontre, il a multiplié les courses, cherchant à chaque fois à combiner avec Rayan Cherki et Gvardiol. Il n’a ménagé aucun effort, aidant la défense sur les offensives adverses durant tout le match. Il sort sur blessure à la 86e minute de jeu, remplacé par McAidoo. Iliman a laissé une bonne impression de vivacité et de percussion, malgré qu’il n’ait pas été décisif. Une confiance absolue de Maresca Sa titularisation précoce confirme la confiance de son coach envers l’ancien numéro 10 des Toffees. Avant la rencontre, Maresca n’avait pas caché son enthousiasme à l’égard du Sénégalais : « Il est tellement bon ! En deux jours à peine, on voit déjà à quel point il est fort dans le un-contre-un, dans le dernier tiers, dans la surface. Je suis très heureux de l’avoir avec nous. » Profitant de l’absence de l’ailier belge Doku, blessé au mollet depuis la Community Shield face à Arsenal, l’attaquant sénégalais a l’opportunité de s’installer durablement dans ce onze des Citizens, où seuls les plus performants et décisifs conserveront leur place. Yaya SOW

items.title: Cyberattaque géante à Berlin : 5,8 téraoctets de données sensibles publiés sur le darknet
items.description: Le groupe de hackers Rhysida a publie sur le darknet les donnees volees lors d'une cyberattaque contre l'infrastructure informatique de l'administration berlinoise, rapporte le journal Bild le 4 septembre. Selon les autorites allemandes, environ 1,44 million de fichiers, representant pres de 5,8 teraoctets, ont ete mis en ligne apres l'expiration de l'ultimatum adresse au Land de Berlin. Rhysida affirme avoir derobe plus de 46 000 contrats, environ 5 900 mots de passe, 16 400 adresses e-mail et 5 000 dossiers personnels d'employes. Parmi les donnees divulguees figurent egalement des documents confidentiels relatifs a des infrastructures critiques et a la securite de la capitale allemande, ainsi que des plans de lutte contre les menaces chimiques, biologiques, radiologiques et nucleaires, et des analyses de vulnerabilite du reseau d'approvisionnement en eau de Berlin. D'apres le Berliner Zeitung , un large eventail de documents confidentiels issus du secteur de la sante a egalement ete rendu public : des dossiers de reeducation, des copies numerisees d'une carte d'invalidite, des rapports d'accidents, des certificats d'incapacite de travail et des avis medicaux. Les noms visibles des dossiers dans la fuite indiquent que la correspondance professionnelle par e-mail concernant les arrets de travail et les vaccinations est egalement concernee. Parmi les fichiers divulgues figurent egalement des scans de resultats de tests PCR. L'attaque contre le reseau informatique berlinois s'est produite entre le 7 et le 12 août et a ete rendue publique le 14 août. Les pirates ont notamment accede aux systemes de plusieurs administrations du Senat de Berlin, dont celles chargees des transports, de l'environnement, du developpement urbain et de la construction. Rhysida avait exige une rancon de 30 bitcoins, soit environ deux millions d'euros, en menacant de publier les donnees volees en cas de refus. Le gouvernement du Land de Berlin, dirige par Kai Wegner, a refuse de payer, affirmant qu'il ne cederait pas au chantage. Le journal Bild a averti que certaines informations pourraient presenter un interet pour les terroristes et les services secrets etrangers.

items.title: Le président de la République a reçu Cheikh Ndiguel Sène
items.description: Le Président de la République, Son Excellence Monsieur Bassirou Diomaye Faye, a reçu ce samedi 5 septembre, Cheikh Ndiguel Sène, informe les services de communication de la présidence de la République . « Le Président de la République a rappelé que l'État entend s'appuyer sur ces relais dans sa politique en direction de la jeunesse. Les guides religieux touchent des enfants et des jeunes que les dispositifs publics n'atteignent pas toujours, et leur contribution à la cohésion nationale reste déterminante », rapporte la même source. Le guide religieux Cheikh Ndiguel Sène consacre son action à l’éducation spirituelle et morale des âmes, avec une attention particulière portée à la jeunesse. Sa notoriété et son influence en font une figure largement écoutée et suivie. À travers ses enseignements, son engagement et sa démarche, il constitue une véritable source d’inspiration et de guidance pour de nombreux disciples qui se reconnaissent dans sa philosophie et adhèrent à sa vision. Il constitue dès lors un véritable vecteur d’éducation, d’encadrement et d’orientation de la jeunesse, particulièrement dans un monde marqué par la multiplication des tentations et des dérives. Le Chef de l'État a dés lors salué ce travail de terrain, mené auprès de familles et de communautés qui comptent sur ces foyers pour instruire, encadrer et transmettre, souligne la source.

items.title: First Lady urges Nigerians to act on charity, not just talk
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru, Abuja The First Lady Senator Oluremi Tinubu has called on Nigerians to move beyond rhetoric and translate the spirit of the International Day of Charity into concrete action for the vulnerable. The First Lady, in her message to mark the 2026 International Global Day of Charity, said charity “is more than giving; it is about extending a helping hand, restoring hope, and supporting those in need.” “As the world marks International Day of Charity 2026, we are reminded of the power of kindness, compassion, and generosity in building a more caring and inclusive society,” she said. She stressed that every act of kindness, however small, can meaningfully change another person’s life. The president’s wife urged citizens to embrace giving and volunteerism, particularly toward the less privileged, as a collective route to reducing poverty and strengthening communities. “Through our collective action, we can help reduce poverty, strengthen our communities, and ensure that no one is left behind,” she said. The message comes as Mrs Tinubu continues to front social-welfare initiatives, including the zonal rollout of the National Community Food Bank Programme in the South-South, which targets pregnant women, lactating mothers and children under six. In Calabar on Friday, she announced cash support for fire victims at Calabar Mall and for women’s groups, underscoring the administration’s push to pair symbolism with material relief. The post First Lady urges Nigerians to act on charity, not just talk appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Action gouvernementale : la reddition des comptes fragilisée par la confusion des responsabilités
items.description: Une note d’analyse publiée par le Centre africain des études stratégiques et de la digitalisation (CAESD) met en lumière les ressorts d’une confusion persistante dans le débat public marocain. Selon ses auteurs, l’une des principales sources de cette ambiguïté réside dans l’absence d’une distinction nette entre l’orientation stratégique, le choix gouvernemental et l’exécution administrative. En ce sens, l'étude met en garde contre les conséquences d’une telle situation, notamment lorsque les orientations royales sont invoquées pour soustraire le gouvernement à ses responsabilités en matière de conception, de décision et de gestion des politiques publiques. Ainsi, le document rappelle que la Constitution marocaine établit une répartition précise des compétences entre les différentes institutions de l’État. Chaque acteur institutionnel dispose ainsi d’un champ d’intervention défini afin d’assurer la continuité de l’action publique. Le Conseil des ministres constitue le cadre de délibération des orientations stratégiques et des lois-cadres, tandis que le gouvernement, responsable devant le Parlement, exerce le pouvoir exécutif, élabore les politiques sectorielles et veille à leur mise en œuvre. Pour sa part, le Parlement est chargé de la fonction législative et du contrôle de l’action gouvernementale, alors que les partis politiques assurent des missions d’encadrement et participent à l’exercice du pouvoir. Pour les auteurs de l’étude, cette architecture constitutionnelle exclut toute possibilité d’exonérer le gouvernement de ses responsabilités. Lorsqu’un discours royal appelle à la réforme de l’enseignement, à la généralisation de la protection sociale ou à l’amélioration du climat de l’investissement, ces objectifs acquièrent le statut de priorités nationales. En revanche, la définition des instruments d’action, l’allocation des ressources budgétaires, la fixation des échéances, l’élaboration des indicateurs de suivi ainsi que la coordination de leur mise en œuvre relèvent exclusivement de la responsabilité du gouvernement et des institutions compétentes précise le document. Dès lors, tout échec d’un programme doit être évalué à l’aune de sa conception, de son exécution et de son pilotage, plutôt qu’à travers une simple réaffirmation de la pertinence de l’orientation stratégique qui l’a inspiré. La note relève également ce qu’elle décrit comme une dérive au sein d’une partie de la pratique partisane. Celle-ci consiste à considérer les orientations royales comme des programmes exécutifs achevés, plaçant les partis dans une posture d’interprétation ou d’accompagnement plutôt que dans un rôle de production de politiques publiques. Les programmes électoraux et les discours politiques mettent alors l’accent sur l’adhésion aux grands chantiers royaux sans préciser les contributions propres des partis, les choix qu’ils proposent ni les résultats dont ils assument la responsabilité. Selon l’étude, cette logique contribue progressivement à estomper les différences entre les formations politiques. L’alternance gouvernementale tend alors à se réduire à une compétition portant sur la gestion d’une même orientation stratégique, à travers des outils et un discours similaires. Le rapport estime que cette pratique affaiblit l’action politique à trois niveaux étroitement liés. Elle prive d’abord les élections de leur fonction fondamentale, qui consiste à départager des programmes distincts. Elle permet ensuite au gouvernement de rattacher ses décisions à une référence supérieure plutôt que de les défendre comme des choix politiques assumés. Enfin, elle expose l’ensemble des institutions de l’État aux conséquences des politiques sectorielles, quelle que soit l’origine réelle des dysfonctionnements, rendant plus difficile l’identification des responsabilités et repoussant l’exercice de la reddition des comptes. Les auteurs soulignent par ailleurs que toutes les décisions gouvernementales ne procèdent pas nécessairement d’orientations émanant des plus hautes institutions de l’État. De même, toute nomination administrative ne traduit pas systématiquement un choix institutionnel centralisé. La note insiste sur le fait que les difficultés rencontrées par un projet public ne doivent pas être automatiquement imputées au sommet de l’État, dès lors que les lois, les administrations et les organismes compétents disposent de prérogatives effectives. Ignorer cette réalité, fait observer, l’analyse, revient à affaiblir l’État lui-même, en réduisant les institutions constitutionnelles à de simples structures d’exécution et en faisant des plus hautes autorités du pays l’unique interlocuteur auprès duquel les citoyens attendent à la fois des solutions et des explications. The post Action gouvernementale : la reddition des comptes fragilisée par la confusion des responsabilités appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Brian Lara joins cricket legends in call for proper medical care for Imran Khan
items.description: West Indies batting great Brian Lara on Saturday joined an international appeal for proper medical treatment and dignified conditions for imprisoned former Pakistan captain and prime minister Imran Khan, saying the issue was one of “basic humanity”, rather than politics. Last month, 22 international cricketers, including 21 ex-captains, wrote a letter to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif appealing for the ex-premier’s medical treatment in line with recent Supreme Court directives. The letter’s signatories included Michael Atherton, Alex Blackwell, Allan Border, Michael Brearley and Greg Chappell, among others. In a statement posted on his official Instagram account, Lara said he and Imran had crossed paths only a handful of times on the cricket field, but the respect he had for the 1992 World Cup-winning captain was “instant and lasting”. View this post on Instagram “I am struggling to understand how someone who was once a beacon of hope, pride and inspiration for his country, at the height of his sporting career, could now find himself in a situation where he is not being cared for and treated with the compassion and dignity he deserves,” Lara wrote. He said he stood with fellow former international captains in calling for Imran to be provided with “proper, independent medical care and the dignity every human being deserves”. “This isn’t politics. It’s basic humanity for a legend of our game,” Lara said. Imran has been in jail since August 2023, convicted in a string of cases that he says were politically driven following his ouster in a 2022 parliamentary vote. There has been much ado over his health in recent months, with him having been taken to the hospital multiple times for an eye ailment — right central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) — that came to light in late January. Meanwhile, his party, the PTI, and the government have been engaged in a blame game , with the former accusing the latter of a lack of transparency in not ensuring appropriate treatment for Imran. On August 18, the Supreme Court directed the government to move Imran to Islamabad’s Shifa International Hospital, a private facility, within two days for examination and treatment by a multidisciplinary medical board. However, it later turned out that Imran was instead taken to the government-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims). Meanwhile, it was also reported that he could not undergo a recommended computed tomography angiography (CTA) at Pims as the required facilities were unavailable at the hospital.

items.title: Nwaneri helps Dortmund to comeback win on Bundesliga debut
items.description: Arsenal loanee Ethan Nwaneri provoked a late own goal as Borussia Dortmund come from two down to win 3-2 at Hoffenheim in a topsy-turvy Bundesliga clash on Saturday. Hoffenheim were the better team for the opening hour but lost their way as Dortmund clicked into gear and romped to victory with three goals in the final 30 minutes. Hoffenheim were two up with 54 minutes played thanks to goals from Leon Avdullahu and Tim Lemperle. Nwaneri, the youngest player in Premier League history, arrived on a season-long loan from Arsenal on deadline day and came on with half an hour played after an injury for Filippo Mane. Striker Serhou Guirassy gave the hosts hope when he scored just after the hour mark and then set up Fabio Silva five minutes later. With just four minutes of regular time remaining, Nwaneri cut down the left and shot centrally, but his effort took a big deflection off home defender Albian Hajdari and into the goal. Bundesliga newcomers Elversberg continued their excellent top-flight arrival with a 4-3 win at Borussia Moenchengladbach, making it two wins from two this season. Gladbach took the lead twice and were 3-1 up midway through the second-half, but Elversberg fought back despite losing manager Vincent Wagner to a second yellow card just before the break. With 10 minutes left, Felix Keidel levelled the scores at 3-3 and Maurice Krattenmacher put the visitors in front in stoppage time with his second goal of the match. Elversberg, with a population of just 13,000, are the smallest town ever to have a German top-flight side but opened the season with a shock 3-2 win over Bayer Leverkusen last week. Leverkusen rebounded from that disappointment by putting sorry Union Berlin to the sword in a 4-0 home victory. Argentina internationals Equi Fernandez and Facundo Medina had Leverkusen 2-0 up at half-time. England centre-back Jarell Quansah set up Patrik Schick for Leverkusen’s third before Ibrahim Maza added a stylish fourth late on. Elsewhere, West Ham loanee Niclas Fuellkrug scored his second goal in three games since returning to Germany to help Werder Bremen win at home 3-1 against RB Leipzig. The Germany striker scored a long-range header, with Eren Dinkci and Marco Gruell also getting on the scoresheet. Europa League finalists Freiburg continued their perfect start to the season with a solid 1-0 win away at promoted Paderborn. Defending champions Bayern Munich face promoted Schalke later on Saturday. AFP The post Nwaneri helps Dortmund to comeback win on Bundesliga debut appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Suspect in Gizri acid attack case arrested in Punjab: police
items.description: A suspect who allegedly attacked a woman with acid in Karachi’s Upper Gizri area recently has been arrested, South Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Syed Asad Raza said on Saturday. A 35-year-old woman suffered burns when a man threw acid on her on Thursday. She was moved to the Burns Centre at Dr Ruth Pfau Civil Hospital Karachi in an Edhi ambulance for treatment. The senior police official said the suspect had fled to his native Rajanpur in Punjab, where he was apprehended with the help of Sindh Police. DIG Raza added that he had written to the Karachi additional inspector general of police to approach the Sindh Home Department for permission to send a police team to Rajanpur and bring the suspect back to Karachi. Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed earlier told Dawn that the victim suffered burns over 15 per cent of her body, affecting her face, neck and abdomen. The victim worked at a bungalow in Clifton and was returning home when the suspect attacked her. Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar had taken notice of the incident and had sought an immediate and had directed police to use all available resources to ensure the immediate arrest of the suspect and take legal action to bring him to justice. The Supreme Court in June this year declared acid attacks more heinous than homicide, describing them as crimes that condemn victims to a “living death”.

items.title: Haaland heads unconvincing Man City top of Premier League
items.description: Erling Haaland maintained Manchester City’s perfect start to the Premier League season but Enzo Maresca’s men were made to sweat for a 1-0 victory over newly-promoted Coventry at the Etihad on Saturday. Maresca was able to unleash Enzo Fernandez and Iliman Ndiaye after their arrivals completed a record outlay by any club of £460 million ($622 million) in the transfer market to refresh the City squad after Pep Guardiola’s decade in charge. The Maresca era has started with three consecutive Premier League wins, but it was a far from perfect performance as the hosts needed a pair of late saves from Gianluigi Donnarumma to deny Coventry a first top-flight point for 25 years. Haaland’s header midway through the first half proved decisive for his third goal in as many games this season. Fernandez was supposed to start on the bench after completing his £125 million move from Chelsea to match the Premier League transfer record. However, an injury to Nico O’Reilly in the warm-up meant the Argentine was thrust into the starting line-up. Ndiaye was also handed his City debut by Maresca alongside Haaland, Antoine Semenyo and Rayan Cherki in a fearsome front four. Coventry had failed to even score in three consecutive defeats to mark their return to the top flight after over two decades away. Yet, Frank Lampard’s men could not have come closer to breaking their duck early on thanks to a gift from Donnarumma. The giant Italian miscontrolled a backpass and recovered to clear off his own line with inches to spare. Taiwo Awoniyi and Jack Rudoni also missed big chances to give the visitors the lead before City began to find their stride. Cherki smashed off the post before Fernandez was involved in the opening goal. His pass fed Semenyo sprinting down the right and his cross was hung up perfectly for Haaland to head home at the back post. The Norwegian was denied a second by Carl Rushworth before half-time, but City failed to build on their advantage and were left clinging on for the three points. Donnarumma was needed to produce two huge saves to deny Loum Tchaouna and Ellis Simms an equaliser and a historic moment for Coventry. Yet, despite another defeat, there was plenty of encouragement for Lampard that Coventry can compete back in the big time. Maresca will know City will need to be much improved when they travel to local rivals Manchester United next weekend. But City do move to the top of the table ahead of champions Arsenal’s clash against Chelsea on Sunday. AFP The post Haaland heads unconvincing Man City top of Premier League appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: France : Rachida Dati va réintégrer la magistrature à quelques jours de son procès pour corruption
items.description: L'ancienne ministre et actuelle maire du VIIe arrondissement de Paris, Rachida Dati, doit comparaître a partir du 16 septembre devant le tribunal correctionnel de Paris dans l'affaire Renault-Nissan, aux cotes notamment de l'ancien patron du groupe automobile, Carlos Ghosn. Selon les informations rapportees par les medias, Rachida Dati a demande a etre reintegree dans la magistrature. Gerald Darmanin a accepte cette demande et propose sa nomination a un poste de premiere substitute a l'administration centrale de la justice a Paris, une fonction presentee comme particulierement recherchee. La procedure doit encore passer devant le Conseil superieur de la magistrature (CSM), dont l'avis est consultatif. La nomination pourra ensuite etre decidee par le ministre de la Justice, avant d'etre formellement signee par le president de la Republique Emmanuel Macron. Une nomination a quelques jours d'un proces sensible Le calendrier de cette reintegration est au cœur des critiques. Rachida Dati doit en effet etre jugee pour corruption et trafic d'influence dans le dossier Renault-Nissan. L'ancienne deputee europeenne est soupconnee d'avoir percu environ 900 000 euros d'une filiale de Renault-Nissan en echange d'activites de lobbying au Parlement europeen. L'accusation estime qu'elle aurait ainsi defendu, contre remuneration et de maniere dissimulee, les interets du constructeur automobile. Rachida Dati conteste ces accusations et affirme avoir realise des prestations d'avocate parfaitement legales. Elle encourt jusqu'a dix ans d'emprisonnement ainsi qu'une peine d'ineligibilite pouvant atteindre cinq ans. Les magistrats denoncent un « message contradictoire » La decision provoque des interrogations au sein de la magistrature. Ludovic Friat, president de l'Union syndicale des magistrats (USM), principal syndicat de magistrats, a estime que cette reintegration envoyait un signal difficilement comprehensible. Alors que l'institution judiciaire fait regulierement l'objet de critiques de la part de responsables politiques, notamment sur les questions de deontologie et de responsabilite des magistrats, une telle nomination « a quelques jours d'un proces penal mediatique concernant l'interessee » constituerait, selon lui, un « message contradictoire ». La polemique est d'autant plus sensible que le nom de Rachida Dati apparaît egalement dans d'autres dossiers judiciaires, actuellement a des stades moins avances de la procedure. Son retour dans la magistrature intervient ainsi au moment ou l'ancienne ministre se retrouve au centre de plusieurs enjeux judiciaires et politiques, alors qu'elle est egalement candidate a la mairie de Paris.

items.title: At least two dead in blast at Bolivia military barracks
items.description: At least two people have been killed after an explosion at a military barracks in Bolivia—but authorities fear the toll could be higher. Bolivian Defence Minister Ernesto Justiniano said at least 81 people had been injured when “pyrotechnic material” detonated at the barracks, where an artillery regiment was stationed, at about 14:30 local time (18:30 GMT) on Friday. Fourteen others remain missing. Health official Rita Nebraska told local television between 10 and 15 people were believed to have died in the incident in Viacha, about 30km (19 miles) from La Paz, according to Reuters. Police said dozens of homes had been damaged by the blast and that emergency workers were searching the rubble. Nebraska said there was a risk of a further explosion and urged people to stay at least 150m from the military base. Base commander Colonel Antonio Amaru told reporters on Saturday that a sergeant and 13 conscripted soldiers aged between 18 and 19-years-old were among the missing. Bolivia’s President Rodrigo Paz expressed his “deepest solidarity” with the families of those who had died and had been injured. He wrote on social media that a “thorough, technical, and transparent investigation” would take place into what happened. Police spokesman Roger Roca told news agency AFP that fireworks had been stored at the barracks and the cause of the blast remained under investigation. Viacha’s authorities have declared three days of mourning.

items.title: Tate brothers officially indicted with trafficking and sex crimes in Romania
items.description: Romanian prosecutors have officially indicted social media influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate with a range of trafficking and sex offenses. They are accused of making more than $1.2m (£888,000) by coercing a girl to perform sex acts on video chats, according to the Romanian Directorate for Investigating Crime and Terrorism (DIICOT). Andrew, 39, is charged with trafficking minors, money laundering, and having sex with a minor. Tristan, 38, is charged with complicity in trafficking in minors and money laundering. The Tates—currently in a Miami jail fighting extradition to the UK over separate charges—deny all the allegations. The brothers—former kickboxers with dual US and British citizenship—have been under criminal investigation in Romania since December 2022. They have been mainly based there since 2017, drawing a large social media audience – many of them young men—through misogynistic messages and images of a luxury lifestyle. Romanian prosecutors described a case as centring on a vulnerable female who was 15 at the time of the alleged offence, in information released on Friday. She is alleged to have been recruited by Andrew and housed in a building in Luton, Bedfordshire, so he could sexually exploit her. Tristan is alleged to have been an accessory, prosecutors say, using physical aggression to coerce the victim. DIICOT investigators allege Andrew controlled her through surveillance and physical aggression and coerced her to perform sex acts on video chats for his financial gain. Andrew is also accused of moving her to Romania to carry on exploiting her in two of his homes. He is separately charged with having sex with a minor, who was 15, in Romania. Prosecutors have also requested four of the brothers’ luxury cars worth £710,000 be confiscated. They believe money was laundered through their purchase. The two brothers were previously indicted in Romania on trafficking charges, but in 2024 an appeals court in Bucharest sent the case back to prosecutors after deeming some evidence inadmissible. It is not yet clear if DIICOT will seek their extradition from the US, and the indictment has to be examined by a judge before any trial can begin. The Tates have denied all the allegations and say their online personas are not their real personalities. Their lawyer in Romania, Eugen Constantin Vidineac, said, “Today’s decision by DIICOT does not determine guilt, and it should not be presented as though it does. It represents the prosecution’s latest attempt to bring this case before a court following the failure of its previous indictment to proceed to trial. “The history of these proceedings matters. The previous indictment was subjected to judicial scrutiny, and the court identified significant irregularities which prevented the case from moving forward to trial. “DIICOT has now chosen to file a new indictment. We will examine every aspect of it with the same level of scrutiny, and we will challenge any evidential, procedural, or legal deficiencies through the appropriate judicial process. “Our clients continue to reject the allegations against them. They have the right to the presumption of innocence, the right to properly examine the evidence relied upon against them, and the right to mount an effective defense.”

items.title: Russia and Ukraine agree not to strike capitals during talks with US envoys
items.description: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner were in Moscow Saturday and expected to head to Kyiv the next day, with Russia and Ukraine vowing not to strike each others’ capitals during talks on ending more than four years of war. Read Also: US President Donald Trump earlier said his son-in-law Kushner and business ally Witkoff were bringing “a proposal to end the war”. The envoys are expected to head for their first visit to Kyiv Sunday, in Washington’s latest bid to break a diplomatic stalemate in Europe’s deadliest conflict since World War II. Both the Kremlin and Kyiv vowed not to strike their main cities during the talks, after months of escalating attacks. “The Russian president, the commander-in-chief, has given the order from midnight tonight not to strike Kyiv for three days,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky — who had offered a truce during the US visits — later said he had spoken to the US envoys and also promised Kyiv would not strike Moscow. “From now through the end of Saturday, as well as on Sunday and Monday, Ukraine is ready to refrain from strikes on Moscow,” Zelensky said on social media. The Ukrainian leader said the US officials have “already begun working with the Russian side today.” Earlier, he accused Russia of trying to disrupt their visit with overnight strikes on Kyiv’s two airports, as well as on a civilian target in the Dnipro region that killed five people. “Clearly, these Russian strikes on the airports are a reaction to the discussions and preparations for the possibility of the US side using an aircraft to travel to Ukraine,” Zelensky said on X. It will be the first time that Witkoff and Kushner visit Kyiv since Trump returned to office last year with a pledge to resolve the conflict. Travelling to Kyiv by plane would be a highly unusual move, with Ukrainian airspace closed since 2022 because of the war. Visiting leaders and officials have generally travelled by train. The envoys are expected in Kyiv on Sunday, a senior Ukrainian official told AFP, while US outlet Axios reported they would meet Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Saturday. Trump told reporters the envoys would seek to gauge whether progress towards peace was possible. Peace efforts have stalled, in part because of Washington’s war with Iran, while Moscow and Kyiv have intensified long-range attacks, driving up civilian casualties to levels not seen since the start of fighting in February 2022. “I sent Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, two great negotiators. They’ve done a great job, and we sent them over to see whether or not we can get something done. And there may be a good chance that we’ll do it,” Trump said. The US president would not say whether the plan the envoys were bringing involved Ukraine ceding territory as he has previously suggested, but added: “We have an idea for peace.” Witkoff and Kushner, who have been involved in negotiations for ceasefires in Gaza and Iran, have travelled repeatedly to Moscow in previous attempts at diplomacy. Grinding war The renewed push for diplomacy comes as Russia and Ukraine pummel each other with long-range missile and drone attacks. Just hours before Trump’s announcement on Friday, a Russian drone struck the headquarters of Ukraine’s SBU security service in central Kyiv, according to Zelensky. The strike, which Zelensky said was aimed at the office of the agency’s acting chief, was the first on its headquarters since the start of Russia’s offensive. Overnight, a Russian strike killed five people and wounded five others in the southeastern city of Kamianske, said Oleksandr Ganzha, head of the Dnipropetrovsk regional military administration. Witkoff and Kushner’s visit comes after a rare trip to Moscow last month by CIA director John Ratcliffe, who warned Russia against any attack on NATO member states, according to US media. Earlier this week, the United States welcomed the Russian finance minister at a G20 gathering in North Carolina. items.title: US envoys arrive in Moscow ahead of Ukraine talks
items.description: Two of US President Donald Trump’s top envoys have arrived in Moscow ahead of a weekend of talks aimed at accelerating efforts to end the war in Ukraine. Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will hold talks in the Russian capital before travelling to Kyiv on Sunday for discussions with Ukraine. Trump told reporters on Friday that Witkoff and Kushner were “bringing with them a proposal to end the war”. So far, efforts from the US and its allies to broker a peace deal have failed to deliver a breakthrough. Both Russia and Ukraine have said they will halt strikes on each others’ capital cities for three days while the delegation conducts its visit. Zelensky said on Saturday that he had spoken to the envoys, who have “already begun working with the Russian side today”. “The plan for tomorrow’s diplomatic engagements in Kyiv, involving the US team, has been approved. We are waiting for Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and are ready for a substantive conversation,” he added. “From now through the end of Saturday, as well as on Sunday and Monday, Ukraine is ready to refrain from strikes on Moscow, and we expect the Russians to do the same regarding Kyiv.” Russian state media reported that President Vladimir Putin had ordered a halt to strikes on Kyiv for three days due to the US visit. Witkoff and Kushner were pictured being greeted by Russian official Kirill Dmitriev after landing at Moscow’s Vnukovo Airport. Flight tracking data showed a US government plane had travelled from Helsinki, Finland, where it flown to from the US earlier in the day. US news outlet Axios reported that the US envoys would separately meet both Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. Kushner and Witkoff have visited Russia several times, but the talks on Sunday would be the first in Ukraine. Delegations from Ukraine have attended talks in the US over the past 18 months. Earlier on Saturday, Zelensky said Russia had fired “demonstrative” strikes on airports in Kyiv and Boryspil overnight ahead of his planned meeting with the US. Ukraine’s president added: “Clearly, these Russian strikes on the airports are a reaction to the discussions and preparations for the possibility of the US side using an aircraft to travel to Ukraine and land at Kyiv Airport or Boryspil Airport.” Ukraine’s airspace has been closed since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022. Zelensky said on Friday he would guarantee the safety of Russian airspace during the envoys’ visit and called for Russia to do the same for Ukraine. He also said an overnight Russian strike on a civilian building in the Dnipro region killed four people and injured five others. Witkoff and Kushner’s visit to Moscow comes just over a week after a rare visit to the Russian capital by the head of the CIA, John Ratcliffe. There was no official comment from Washington or the Kremlin on what was discussed. Speaking last week, Trump described the meeting as “semi-routine.” Last year, the US, Ukraine and Russia separately suggested that a deal to end the war was edging closer following a flurry of talks brokered by the Americans. European allies also held talks in Paris, but discussions ultimately ended without a breakthrough. Key disagreements remain between the warring sides on issues such as territory and security guarantees for Ukraine. In recent months, both Russia and Ukraine have intensified their aerial attacks as fighting continues. Ukraine said it has struggled to repel attacks due to a lack of interceptor missiles, while Kyiv has focused its strikes on Russian economic infrastructure targets.

items.description: La rentrée scolaire au compte de l’année académique 2026-2027 aura officiellement lieu le 5 octobre prochain. La décision a été annoncée par le dernier Conseil des ministres. La question de la prochaine rentrée scolaire figurait parmi les sujets examinés lors de cette session du Conseil des ministres. Les échanges ont notamment porté sur les dispositions à prendre pour assurer le démarrage des activités scolaires dans les meilleures conditions. Au cours de la réunion, la ministre de l’Éducation nationale, de l’Alphabétisation, de l’Enseignement technique et de la Formation professionnelle, Bintou Kéïta, a également présenté une communication consacrée à la proclamation des résultats de la session de rattrapage du baccalauréat unique 2026 et aux préparatifs de la rentrée scolaire 2026-2027. Le Conseil des ministres a salué les dispositions prises par le département pour conduire à la proclamation, le mercredi 2 septembre 2026, des résultats de la session de rattrapage du baccalauréat. Il a également adressé ses félicitations aux candidats déclarés admis à l’issue de cette session. Les discussions se sont ensuite poursuivies autour des préparatifs de la rentrée, avec un accent particulier sur la rentrée administrative et la date d’ouverture effective des classes. À l’issue des échanges, le gouvernement a finalement retenu la date du 5 octobre 2026 pour la rentrée scolaire 2026-2027, a annoncé le porte-parole du gouvernement, Faya François Bourouno.

items.title: Inter Board Coordination Commission relaxes equivalence criteria for foreign-board students with two science subjects
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Inter Board Coordination Commission (IBCC) on Saturday decided that Science Group equivalence would be awarded to students of foreign boards who had passed at least two science subjects, providing greater flexibility in academic pathways. Similarly, the forum recommended 12 additional Deeni Madaris for equivalence of their qualifications with SSC and HSSC, bringing the total number of institutions under the equivalence framework to 26. It also agreed to include B-Form/CNIC numbers on SSC and HSSC certificates, making academic records easier to identify, access and verify. Additionally, the commission will offer scholarships and overseas exposure opportunities to board toppers, besides arranging winter and summer camps for high-achieving students to provide them with broader learning, leadership and exposure opportunities. These decisions were made during the 184th IBCC Forum meeting in Murree. “The two-day IBCC Forum concluded in Murree with a series of important decisions aimed at transforming Pakistan’s examination system from rote learning towards conceptual assessment, while improving transparency, uniformity and international recognition of Pakistani qualifications,” a press release said. It added that chairpersons from Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education (BISEs) across the country, technical education boards, and senior representatives of curriculum and textbook boards had come together for the meeting. According to the press release, National Coordinator of the IBCC Forum Inayatullah Waseem emphasised the importance of active participation and collective ownership of examination reforms. He said the IBCC Forum provided an important national platform for boards to learn from one another, share successful practices and develop common solutions to challenges faced by the examination system. The national coordinator also stressed that greater coordination among boards and consistent implementation of agreed reforms were essential for ensuring fairness, quality and public confidence in examinations across the country. “A major focus of the forum was the implementation of the prime minister’s directives for standardisation of the examination system across the country. The forum adopted measures for greater uniformity in assessment and examination practices, which will also support the credibility and international recognition of Pakistani qualifications,” the press release said. It stated that the forum was informed that examination boards in Sindh, the Federal Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education (FBISE), the AJK Board, the KIU Board, the Aga Khan Board and the Ziauddin Board had implemented the new grading policy, under which the minimum passing marks had been increased to 40 per cent. Awareness sessions and workshops would also be organised to facilitate implementation of the revised grading formula across the country. Meanwhile, the forum agreed to develop a uniform calendar for theory and practical examinations and formulate common guidelines and procedures for practical examinations to ensure greater consistency, fairness and transparency across examination boards. During the meeting, BISE Kohat, BISE Quetta and FBISE presented their best practices, innovative initiatives and outcomes for possible adoption and replication by other boards. Speaking on examination reforms, IBCC Executive Director Dr Ghulam Ali Mallah appreciated the Punjab government for the merit-based appointment of chairpersons of examination boards. He observed that competent professional leadership was adding value to the IBCC Forum and strengthening the national effort to shift examinations from rote learning towards conceptual assessment. Dr Mallah also appreciated the Sindh government and chairpersons of Sindh examination boards for implementing e-marking across the province, describing it as an important step towards greater transparency, efficiency and credibility in the examination system. He emphasised that the reforms being pursued through the IBCC Forum were part of a broader national effort to develop an examination system that tests understanding rather than memory, rewards genuine learning, embraces technology, and strengthens the national and international credibility of Pakistani qualifications.

items.title: Two teenage terrorists surrender, 11-year-old female captive rescued
items.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri Two teenage members of a terrorist group have surrendered to troops of Sector 3 Operation Hadin Kai in Monguno Local Government Area of Borno State. Likewise, troops of 82 Division Task Force Battalion have rescued an 11-year-old girl who was allegedly abducted and taken from her community for a suspected spying mission in Gwoza Local Government Area of Borno State. This comes as troops of 101 Special Forces Battalion have arrested a 60-year-old man suspected of being an Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) spy along the Cross Kanwa road in Kukawa Local Government Area of the state. Information obtained from credible security sources which was corroborated by a security analyst in Lake Chad, Zagazola Makama, revealed that the two, identified as Umar Mohammed, 17, and Aliu Hassan, 13, surrendered at about 7:15 a.m. on Sept. 4, 2026, to troops deployed at Charlie 7 in Monguno town. The youths reportedly surrendered with one wristwatch and a catapult. “Preliminary interrogation revealed that the two had escaped from a terrorist camp in Martab, Marte Local Government Area, citing harsh living conditions at the camp. “The surrendered youths and recovered items are currently in the custody of Headquarters Sector 3 Military Intelligence Branch for further necessary action. “The development adds to ongoing efforts by security forces to encourage members of terrorist groups to abandon violence and surrender to authorities,” a source said. In another development, troops of 82 Division Task Force Battalion have rescued an 11-year-old girl who was allegedly abducted and taken from her community for a suspected spying mission in Gwoza Local Government Area of Borno State. Identified as Miss Aisha Mustafa, was rescued at about 1:41 a.m. on Sept. 4, 2026, during a routine patrol around the Armuda general area. According to the sources, the girl was among three persons allegedly taken from Mountain Village of Saha by two suspected terrorists. Preliminary investigation indicated that the terrorists allegedly intended to use the victims to monitor the activities of troops deployed around Ngoshe. The sources said that “upon sighting the troops, Aisha fled towards them and surrendered, while the other two individuals reportedly fled back towards the village”. The rescued girl is currently receiving necessary assistance as efforts are ongoing to reunite her with her family members. Additionally, troops of 101 Special Forces Battalion have arrested a 60-year-old man suspected of being an Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) spy along the Cross-Kukawa road in Kukawa Local Government Area of Borno State. The suspect, identified as Mallam Garba Audi, was arrested at about 9:55 a.m. on Sept. 3, 2026. The arrest followed human intelligence indicating the possible movement of an ISWAP spy from Monguno towards Kukawa. “Acting on the information, troops intensified surveillance around their defensive location and arrested Audi, who was reportedly found wandering aimlessly along the Cross-Kukawa road. “During preliminary investigation, the suspect claimed to have lost his way from Digimari in northern Borno. “Troops recovered cement bags containing clothing and mosquito nets from the suspect. “The suspect and recovered items are currently in military custody and are to be transferred to 19 Military Intelligence Regiment for further investigation,” sources revealed. items.title: Sissili/Léo : décès de l’ancien maire et député, Dramane Nignan
items.description: BURKINA-DECES-ANCIEN-MAIRE-DEPUTE-PROVINCE-SISSILI Sissili/Léo : décès de l’ancien maire et député, Dramane Nignan Léo, 4 septembre 2026 (AIB) – La province de la Sissili en deuil suite au décès, survenu ce vendredi 4 septembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, de Dramane Nignan, ancien maire de la commune de Léo et ancien député de la province. Un hommage solennel lui a été rendu à la mairie de Léo, suivi de son inhumation à Dabiou, son village natal. Acteur politique engagé successivement au CDP puis au NTD, l’illustre disparu a également exercé les fonctions de vice-président de l’Assemblée nationale. Sa disparition subite, intervenue aux environs de 3h40 à la suite d’une dégradation rapide de sa santé, a profondément ému ses proches. Son frère cadet, Karim Nignan, témoigne de ses derniers moments : « Hier soir encore, vers 22 heures, nous avons mangé ensemble. Il s’est enquis de tout le monde et a prononcé cette phrase : “J’ai été très bien accompagné”. » Face à l’affluence exceptionnelle et à la suggestion de la communauté musulmane, la famille a opté pour une inhumation dès ce vendredi même. Sur le plan professionnel et politique, la tristesse est partagée par ses collaborateurs et pairs. Josiane Yago/Ziba, qui fut sa secrétaire à la mairie, retient de lui un dirigeant « à l’écoute de ses collaborateurs, engagé pour la cause commune et de la province toute entière, prêt à mettre la main à la poche pour soutenir son prochain ». Le Razan-Naaba Belémwendé de Boudry, président de l'Association des anciens maires du Burkina dont Dramane Nignan était le deuxième vice-président, a salué la mémoire d’un « modèle » et d’un « véritable baobab ». « C’était un personnage important, brutalement arraché à notre affection, qui est toujours resté proche de sa population. Il nous appartient désormais de préserver et de faire fructifier le précieux héritage qu’il laisse derrière lui » a-t-il déclaré. Il a par ailleurs exprimé sa reconnaissance aux autorités locales, notamment le Haut-commissaire, le président de la délégation spéciale (PDS) et le chef de canton de Léo, pour leur soutien indéfectible lors de cet adieu. Agence d’Information du Burkina BAN/ata/zs

items.title: Burkina/Lutte antipaludisme: à Manga le gouvernement donne l’exemple pour la 2e édition des JNLAV
items.description: La deuxième édition des Journées nationales de lutte antivectorielle (JNLAV), qui se tient du 5 au 6 septembre 2026, mobilise les pouvoirs publics et les communautés autour d’un même objectif : réduire les gîtes larvaires et renforcer la prévention du paludisme. À Manga, le ministre de la Santé, Dr Robert Lucien Jean-Claude Kargougou, et le ministre d’État, ministre de l’Agriculture, de l’Eau, des Ressources animales et halieutiques, le Commandant Ismaël Sombié, ont donné l’exemple ce samedi 5 septembre en participant directement aux opérations de terrain. Pelles, brouettes et matériaux de remblai en main, les deux membres du Gouvernement ont pris part aux travaux de destruction des gîtes larvaires sur des sites favorables à la prolifération des moustiques vecteurs du paludisme. Une manière de joindre l’acte à la sensibilisation et de rappeler que la prévention commence aussi dans l’environnement immédiat des populations. Cette deuxième édition intervient dans le prolongement du franc succès enregistré lors de la première édition des JNLAV, tenue les 8 et 9 août 2026. La mobilisation observée à travers le pays avait permis d’intensifier les actions d’assainissement et de destruction des gîtes larvaires, confirmant l’importance d’une approche communautaire dans la lutte contre les maladies à transmission vectorielle. Pour le ministre d’État, Commandant Ismaël Sombié, il importe de maintenir cette dynamique. « Il était de bon ton que nous puissions poursuivre ces efforts cette année », a-t-il indiqué, appelant les populations à s’impliquer davantage dans la destruction des gîtes larvaires et l’assainissement de leur environnement. Remblayer les eaux stagnantes, curer les caniveaux, éliminer les récipients susceptibles de retenir l’eau et assainir les concessions sont autant de gestes qui contribuent à réduire les lieux de ponte des moustiques. À Manga comme dans les autres localités du pays, le Gouvernement appelle ainsi à une mobilisation continue. Car entre deux campagnes, le moustique, lui, ne fait pas de pause. La lutte doit donc se poursuivre chaque jour, dans chaque concession, chaque quartier et chaque communauté. items.title: Réforme du gouvernement : Bah Oury veut secouer la machine et accélérer les résultats
items.description: Face à l’ampleur des chantiers engagés par le gouvernement guinéen, le Premier ministre Amadou Oury Bah entend insuffler un nouveau rythme à l’action publique. Il invite les départements ministériels à sortir du fonctionnement en vase clos et à davantage mutualiser leurs efforts afin d’accélérer la mise en œuvre des priorités nationales. Cette nouvelle approche vise notamment à réduire les lenteurs administratives, limiter les chevauchements de compétences et renforcer la coordination entre les différents ministères. L’objectif est également d’optimiser l’utilisation des ressources publiques et de favoriser une plus grande efficacité dans l’exécution des politiques gouvernementales. Pour le Premier ministre, la transversalité doit désormais devenir un principe central de l’action gouvernementale. Les différents départements sont ainsi appelés à travailler davantage de manière concertée, en dépassant les logiques sectorielles pour privilégier une approche fondée sur les résultats et l’impact concret des décisions prises. À travers cette réforme, le gouvernement entend rapprocher davantage l’action de l’État des préoccupations quotidiennes des citoyens. Une administration mieux coordonnée, plus réactive et davantage orientée vers les résultats doit permettre de transformer plus rapidement les décisions publiques en réalisations concrètes. Cette volonté de changement traduit ainsi une ambition claire : améliorer l’efficacité de l’action gouvernementale, accélérer l’exécution des projets prioritaires et faire de la culture du résultat un véritable marqueur de la gouvernance publique.
